_comment: Branch rules as code for `main`, applied by factory/bin/apply-branch-protection.sh (repo admin; dry-run by default, --apply writes, a second run is a no-op; re-run after any change here). Only real GitHub REST fields live here: `protection` is the body of PUT repos/{r}/branches/{branch}/protection (null: the branch has no classic protection, and one found on GitHub is DELETEd), and each `rulesets` entry is the body of POST/PUT repos/{r}/rulesets (keys starting with `_` are stripped). A rule GitHub cannot express is listed under `unexpressed`, printed on every run, and never silently dropped. Bypass OFF for everyone, admins included: no ruleset names a bypass actor, and the only one ever added is the factory GitHub App, from FACTORY_APP_ID.
_desk_note: specs/factory-step3-v1 TB10 (ticket T29), a desk note under I15: this file replaces factory/policy/branch-protection.json in a desk commit. Until then tests/test_halt_rules.sh reads it here, and make sim's desk applies it to its world (a logged stand-in).
_protection: Step-2 ruling Q2 (specs/factory-step2-v1/RULINGS.md): every rule classic protection held now lives in ruleset `main`, where the App's bypass applies, so post-merge's direct push on the App token is not refused. Classic `required_pull_request_reviews` became the `pull_request` rule, `required_status_checks` the `required_status_checks` rule, `allow_force_pushes: false` the `non_fast_forward` rule, `allow_deletions: false` the `deletion` rule, and `enforce_admins: true` is a ruleset's default (only `bypass_actors` bypass, and there are none). Nothing was left for classic protection.

rulesets.name: main
rulesets._comment: Every rule on main. Parameter names are GitHub's REST ruleset schema (docs.github.com/rest/repos/rules#create-a-repository-ruleset; components repository-rule-*). Required checks are the bare job ids of .github/workflows/gates.yml that report on pull_request and on the queue path (I18; a check run is named by its job id, records/TB0.md (b)), each from GitHub Actions (integration_id 15368); `apply-branch-protection.sh --check` proves the set. Approvals: none required globally; a code owner's review is (CODEOWNERS), and the two-owner rule on the factory's own paths is the required `owners` check (GitHub counts one owner). Merge commits only: post-merge.sh reads the merge commit. The merge_queue rule is sent only when the repo is organization-owned (native-queue: yes): one entry built and merged at a time, merge commits.
rulesets._halt: ADR-0004 options C and D (specs/factory-step3-v1 TB10): adding factory/HALT needs no approval, because .github/workflows/halt.yml commits it onto main with the App, the only bypass actor, never through a PR or the queue; removing it needs two distinct code-owner approvals, counted by the required check `halt-guard`, which reviews.yml re-runs on every review.

unexpressed.rule: factory/HALT: zero approvals to add, two to remove
unexpressed.why: GitHub has no rule keyed on file deletion, and ruleset `required_reviewers` needs a Team, which a user-owned repo has none of. The factory expresses it instead: halt.yml commits factory/HALT with the App (zero approvals, never queued), and the required check `halt-guard` fails a PR deleting it without two distinct code-owner approvals on its head.

unexpressed.rule: two distinct code-owner approvals on factory/**, .adlc/**, .github/**, .claude/** and CODEOWNERS
unexpressed.why: `require_code_owner_review` counts one code owner, and `required_reviewers` needs a Team. The required check `owners` (factory/bin/owners-check.sh) counts two distinct owners' approvals on the PR's current head; until a second owner is in CODEOWNERS no such PR can merge (the spec's rule; Aaron's kit).

unexpressed.rule: only the App merges a ticket PR (the first-party serial queue)
unexpressed.why: A rule cannot be scoped to a PR class, and restricting updates of main to the App (rule `update`) would also stop desk, human and HALT-removal PRs, which the queue does not land. A person can still merge a PR that is up to date with main (strict) and passes every required check, which are the gates the queue runs; the queue lands with the App, the only bypass actor, after the same gates on the merge commit.
